clue.text: Possibly Priti Patel, one notably heartless government representative

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged some other way, so they are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written: the British Conservative politician
taken as written

indicators.note: a heartless word loses everything between its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A jibe that the former Home Secretary Priti Patel is a notably heartless member of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves NY from 'notably'; 'Possibly' shuffles PRITI PATEL, ONE and NY together. Priti Patel was a UK Home Secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: A plenipotentiary is an envoy given full powers to act on behalf of a government.

clue.text: Leader with the respect due to me?

parts.note: pace, from Latin, means with all due respect to someone you disagree with
the crossword setter speaking of themself

explanation.surface: A leader asks whether he deserves my respect.
explanation.walkthrough: In a cryptic, 'me' is often the setter, so SETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacesetter is the one out in front whom others follow, a leader in a race or field.

clue.text: Kind of complex skill star almost elevated

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means the pieces are written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: art means skill

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a celeb is a star

explanation.surface: Someone's skill as a star is almost a complex, raised up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CELEB to CELE; ART + CELE read upwards, as 'elevated' says, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electra complex is a Freudian-era term for a daughter's attachment to her father.

clue.text: Voguish French writer's by southern Scottish city

parts.note: in means fashionable or voguish
Jules Verne was a French writer; with the possessive, VERNES

explanation.surface: A trendy French author lives near a city in southern Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Inverness is in the far north, so 'southern' misleads: it is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverness is the main city of the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: What comes from Iris's topless dancing style

indicators.note: topless means the first letter, the top in a down entry, is removed

parts.note: Morris dancing is a traditional English folk dance

explanation.surface: Iris performs a topless dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Iris is the flower, not a woman. Morris dancing is English folk dancing with bells and sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris root comes from the rhizome of certain irises and is used in perfume.

clue.text: Stared at Rodriguez after close shave, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals that the words are spoken, giving a word that sounds like them

parts.note: Rodriguez (Rodriquez) is the setter, who would call himself I; after a close shave of the head one has been balded

explanation.surface: The setter was stared at after shaving his head.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'I balded' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare hard at them.

clue.text: Conveyances able to return

indicators.note: to return means the word comes back the other way, read backwards

parts.note: smart means clever or able

explanation.surface: Vehicles that can come back.
explanation.definitionFit: Trams are vehicles on rails that carry passengers.

clue.text: Mexican lake-dweller too lax to swim on lake

indicators.note: to swim suggests the letters moving about freely, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Mexican creature too lazy to swim in its lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to swim' shuffles TOO LAX into AXOLOT; L goes below it ('on' in a down entry).
explanation.definitionFit: The axolotl is a salamander native to the lakes around Mexico City.

clue.text: One of the tips of Yuletide long ago

indicators.note: one of two tips means this tip or that one, so the choosing word sits between the two letters
the tips of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: one of two things is one or the other, giving the word for a choice

explanation.surface: Christmas customs from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'One of the tips of Yuletide' as 'Y or E': the two end letters of Yuletide with OR between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Yore means time long past, as in 'days of yore'.

clue.text: Conservative Brexiteer, one making cuts

parts.note: a Brexiteer voted Leave, a leaver

explanation.surface: A Tory who backed Brexit is cutting things.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK's 2016 referendum, Brexit supporters voted Leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaver is a heavy butcher's knife for chopping.

clue.text: Charm possessed by us, after hair recedes

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first
something receding goes backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a mane is a head of hair
what we possess is ours

explanation.surface: We keep our charm even as our hairline goes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recedes' reverses MANE to ENAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour is to captivate or charm someone.

clue.text: Male desiring sex in 24 hours, then 8,760

parts.note: Saturday, SAT, is a day of 24 hours
a year has 8,760 hours, abbreviated YR

explanation.surface: A man wanting sex within a day, then for a whole year.
explanation.walkthrough: 8,760 hours is 365 days, a year.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a lustful man, after the lecherous woodland creatures of Greek myth.

clue.text: See red drop of alcohol's still taken quickly

parts.note: to snap is to lose your temper, see red
a shot is a small drink of spirits

explanation.surface: Losing one's temper over a dram, still drunk fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a photograph, a still image, taken quickly.

clue.text: During plague, libertine gives sign of easing up

indicators.note: during means within, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a blight is a plague
a rake is a libertine

explanation.surface: A womaniser slows down during a pandemic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'libertine' is the old word for a rake, a dissolute man.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake light shows when a driver slows down.

clue.text: Crossing States, cutting through path one's left

indicators.note: cutting through means one piece goes inside another
left means taken away, so the letter goes

parts.note: a trail is a path
one is I, the Roman numeral
avers means states or asserts

explanation.surface: Crossing American states on a trail, one has departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' is a verb, not the USA; 'cutting through' puts it inside the path once 'left' has removed one.
explanation.definitionFit: A traversal is an act of crossing from one side to the other.

clue.text: Propose new packaging area, with a staple for the box

indicators.note: packaging means wrapping one piece around another
new means the word is made fresh, rearranged

explanation.surface: A business plan for new packaging, including a staple for boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns PROPOSE into SOPOPER, which 'packaging' wraps around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap operas are a mainstay of television, 'the box' being slang for TV.

clue.text: Mathematician's logarithmic base rule broken

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reformed

explanation.surface: A mathematician's rule about logarithms has been broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges RULE, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was an 18th-century Swiss mathematician, after whom e is often named.

clue.text: Husband has green bouquet crossing big road

parts.note: eco means environmentally friendly, green

indicators.note: crossing means one word spans the other, holding it inside

parts.note: a wine's bouquet is its nose
the M1 is a major British motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A man carries an eco-friendly bunch of flowers across a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' is a verb. The M1 is England's main north-south motorway; 1 looks like I.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is to manage them carefully, to economise.

clue.text: Character caught by musket hospitalised

indicators.note: caught by means the answer is held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone shot with a musket ends up in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the distinguishing character or spirit of a group or person.

clue.text: Mole maybe with aspiration to be a ruler once

parts.note: aspiration is the breathed sound H
Adrian Mole is the diarist hero of Sue Townsend's books

explanation.surface: A mole with ambitions to rule.
explanation.walkthrough: Adrian Mole is a famous British fictional teenage diarist.
explanation.definitionFit: Hadrian was a Roman emperor, the ruler who built the wall across northern England.

clue.text: Recorded volume of car wheel with caution

parts.note: Audi is a German car make
a wheel is round, like the letter O
in football a referee books a player as a caution

explanation.surface: The volume level of a car wheel, treated warily.
explanation.walkthrough: Booking is the yellow-card caution in British football.
explanation.definitionFit: An audiobook is a book read aloud and recorded.

clue.text: Foul, unacceptable TV channel

parts.note: behaviour that is a bit off is unacceptable
side is old British slang for a TV channel, as in 'the other side'

explanation.surface: A TV channel airing something offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, being offside is an infringement penalised by the referee.
explanation.definitionFit: Offside is a football infringement, a foul in the loose sense of a rule broken.

clue.text: Issues with rabble-rousing delaying leader

indicators.note: the leader, the first letter, is delayed until the end

parts.note: sedition is stirring up rebellion, rabble-rousing

explanation.surface: Problems with a demagogue who keeps the leader waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delaying leader' moves the S of SEDITION to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Editions are issues of a newspaper or book.

clue.text: What's discussed in work penned by jerk

indicators.note: penned by means held inside, as in a pen

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Talk about a work written by a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' looks like an insult but is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject under discussion.

clue.text: Perhaps one's going to darn filthy place

definitions.meaning: one who sews, as when darning
a drain for waste, a filthy place

explanation.surface: Someone about to mend socks in a squalid spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling covers a stitcher and an underground drain.

clue.text: Old King Lear's first to show guts

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia

indicators.note: first means just the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: King Lear's first act lays bare his insides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Lear' wants to be one unit; split it, as Offa is the old king.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the entrails and organs of a slaughtered animal, its guts.

clue.text: Fleece coats from the south

indicators.note: in a down entry, read from the south means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: macs are raincoats

explanation.surface: Fleeces cover the coats of southern sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' is a verb, to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to cheat them, and a scam is a swindle.

clue.text: Cold and hot dish in take-away outlet

parts.note: hip means fashionable, hot
a pie is a dish

explanation.surface: Cold and hot food at a takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: A chippie is British slang for a fish-and-chip shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A chippie is a fish-and-chip shop selling takeaway food.

clue.text: The thing eaten by most of carp or other fish

indicators.note: eaten by means swallowed inside another word
most of means the last letter is lost

parts.note: to carp is to whinge, complain
it means the thing

explanation.surface: Something is swallowed by a carp or another fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' is the verb to complain, not a fish; 'most of' drops its last letter and 'eaten by' puts the thing inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The whiting is a sea fish of the cod family, a fish other than carp.

clue.text: Wild cheering met Man U's weak capitulation in Europe

indicators.note: wild means the letters run riot and rearrange

parts.note: Man U is the nickname of Manchester United football club

explanation.surface: Manchester United fans cheer wildly as their side folds in a European match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' shuffles CHEERING MET and MANU.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1938 Munich Agreement saw Britain and France yield to Hitler over the Sudetenland, a byword for appeasement.
